objective: In gorilla/mux, when two routes share the same path but differ only by their query-parameter constraints (e.g. GET /api?foo=... and GET /api?bar=...), a request that satisfies the SECOND route's query is not matched: Route.Match leaves a stale method-mismatch error set from the first candidate route and returns it instead of clearing it once a later route fully matches. Find the method-mismatch clearing logic in Route.Match and fix it so a request matching any same-path route (regardless of which earlier candidate set a mismatch error) matches cleanly with no MatchErr.

explorationSubQuestions.question: In gorilla/mux Route.Match at this pinned revision, under what exact condition is a previously-set match.MatchErr cleared, and why does that condition drop the case where an EARLIER candidate route set a non-method-mismatch error before a later route fully matches?
explorationSubQuestions.groundTruth: Match only clears match.MatchErr when it equals ErrMethodMismatch and r.handler != nil; it must instead clear on any non-nil MatchErr once the route otherwise matches (the fix changes `== ErrMethodMismatch` to `!= nil`), so a later fully-matching same-path route is not shadowed by a stale error.
